```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Desflurane is a volatile inhalational anaesthetic with a low blood-gas
partition coefficient. Lu 2024 gave seven mechanically ventilated piglets a
fixed 6% inspiratory desflurane concentration for 2 h (uptake) and then 40%
oxygen alone for 2 h (disposition), and followed the end-tidal gas, the
femoral-arterial blood and the pulmonary-artery (mixed venous) blood
concentrations. Blood concentrations were measured by headspace gas
chromatography and, like the gas concentrations, are expressed as percent
vapour (the partial pressure as a volume percent).

Each concentration-time curve was fitted per animal in WinNonlin with a
zero-order (constant-infusion) input over the 120-min uptake phase and
biexponential disposition, i.e. a two-compartment model, and Table 3 reports
the mean (SD) of the individual estimates. The three sites were fitted
independently, so the paper contributes **three** model files:

```{r models}
des_models <- c(
  "Lu_2024_desflurane_pig_endtidal",    # end-tidal gas
  "Lu_2024_desflurane_pig_arterial",    # femoral-arterial blood
  "Lu_2024_desflurane_pig_mixedvenous"  # pulmonary-artery (mixed venous) blood
)
site_label <- c(
  Lu_2024_desflurane_pig_endtidal = "End-tidal",
  Lu_2024_desflurane_pig_arterial = "Arterial blood",
  Lu_2024_desflurane_pig_mixedvenous = "Pulmonary artery blood"
)
mods <- lapply(stats::setNames(des_models, des_models), function(m) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m)))
```

* Citation: `r mods[[1]]$reference`
* Article: [Front Pharmacol 2024;15:1339690](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2024.1339690)

```{r description}
for (m in des_models) {
  cat(m, "\n", sep = "")
  cat(strwrap(mods[[m]]$description, 76), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

# Population

Seven male domestic piglets, 5 months old and weighing 28 +/- 5 kg, were
anaesthetised with intramuscular tiletamine/zolazepam and atropine, maintained
on fentanyl, propofol and pancuronium, tracheostomised and ventilated with 40%
oxygen at a tidal volume of 8 mL/kg (Lu 2024 Sections 2.2-2.3). Desflurane was
delivered through a vaporiser at a 5 L/min fresh-gas flow. Arterial and
pulmonary-artery blood was drawn simultaneously at 1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50,
60, 80, 100 and 120 min of each phase (Section 2.5). End-tidal values below
0.2% were discarded, which truncates the end-tidal curve after about 60 min of
washout (Sections 2.4 and 4.5). No covariates were investigated.

```{r population}
str(mods[["Lu_2024_desflurane_pig_arterial"]]$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries its origin as an in-file comment; the table below
collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Disposition equation `Y = A*exp(-alpha*t) + B*exp(-beta*t)` | n/a | Table 3 footnote |
| Zero-order input over the 120-min uptake phase | n/a | Abstract; Section 4.2; Figure 3 caption |
| **`Lu_2024_desflurane_pig_endtidal`** | | |
| `lcl` | 0.07 L/min | Table 3, end-tidal, Clearance |
| `lvc` | 0.10474 L | derived `CL/k10` from Table 3 end-tidal A, B, alpha and beta half-lives (Table 3 prints 0.10) |
| `lq` | 0.026351 L/min | derived `k12*vc`, Table 3 end-tidal macro-constants |
| `lvp` | 1.7017 L | derived `q/k21`, Table 3 end-tidal macro-constants |
| **`Lu_2024_desflurane_pig_arterial`** | | |
| `lcl` | 0.08 L/min | Table 3, arterial blood, Clearance |
| `lvc` | 0.10349 L | derived `CL/k10` from Table 3 arterial A, B, alpha and beta half-lives (Table 3 prints 1.09; see below) |
| `lq` | 0.020623 L/min | derived `k12*vc`, Table 3 arterial macro-constants |
| `lvp` | 1.0929 L | derived `q/k21`, Table 3 arterial macro-constants |
| **`Lu_2024_desflurane_pig_mixedvenous`** | | |
| `lcl` | 0.09 L/min | Table 3, pulmonary artery blood, Clearance |
| `lvc` | 0.34996 L | derived `CL/k10` from Table 3 pulmonary artery A, B, alpha and beta half-lives (Table 3 prints 0.35) |
| `lq` | 0.038638 L/min | derived `k12*vc`, Table 3 pulmonary artery macro-constants |
| `lvp` | 2.3577 L | derived `q/k21`, Table 3 pulmonary artery macro-constants |
| `addSd` (all three files) | 0 (fixed) | not reported; see Assumptions |

## Reconstructing the parameters from Table 3

Table 3 gives the biexponential macro-constants (A, B and the alpha and beta
half-lives) together with secondary parameters (clearance, central volume,
steady-state volume, mean residence time). The rate constants follow from the
macro-constants alone; the clearance then fixes the scale of the volumes.
The chunk below repeats the derivation from the Table 3 means and, in the
other direction, recovers the macro-constants from the packaged parameters.

```{r derive}
tab3 <- data.frame(
  model = des_models,
  A = c(731.26, 514.32, 147.32),       # %, Table 3
  B = c(3.45, 2.11, 2.10),             # %, Table 3
  thalpha = c(0.75, 0.71, 1.86),       # min, Table 3
  thbeta = c(61.90, 46.39, 61.29),     # min, Table 3
  CL = c(0.07, 0.08, 0.09),            # L/min, Table 3
  Vc = c(0.10, 1.09, 0.35),            # L, Table 3
  Vss = c(1.29, 1.20, 2.75),           # L, Table 3
  MRT = c(15.51, 15.00, 31.26),        # min, Table 3
  cmax = c(5.68, 4.85, 4.07),          # %, Table 3
  aucinf.obs = c(695.88, 603.03, 533.10) # % x min, Table 3
)

# Packaged typical values, read back from each model file
pk <- bind_rows(lapply(des_models, function(m) {
  th <- mods[[m]]$theta
  data.frame(
    model = m,
    cl = exp(th[["lcl"]]), vc = exp(th[["lvc"]]),
    q = exp(th[["lq"]]), vp = exp(th[["lvp"]])
  )
}))

recovered <- pk |>
  mutate(
    k10 = cl / vc, k12 = q / vc, k21 = q / vp,
    s = k10 + k12 + k21, p = k10 * k21,
    alpha = (s + sqrt(s^2 - 4 * p)) / 2,
    beta = (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * p)) / 2
  ) |>
  left_join(tab3, by = "model") |>
  mutate(
    # nominal input amount implied by the fit: A + B = dose / vc
    dose = vc * (A + B),
    A_rec = dose / vc * (alpha - k21) / (alpha - beta),
    B_rec = dose / vc * (k21 - beta) / (alpha - beta),
    thalpha_rec = log(2) / alpha,
    thbeta_rec = log(2) / beta,
    Vss_rec = vc + vp,
    MRT_rec = Vss_rec / cl,
    # central volume implied by the PRINTED Vss and MRT with the macro-constants
    Vc_check = Vss * (A / (log(2) / thalpha) + B / (log(2) / thbeta)) / ((A + B) * MRT)
  )

recovered |>
  transmute(
    Site = site_label[model],
    A = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", A, A_rec),
    B = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", B, B_rec),
    `alpha t1/2 (min)` = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", thalpha, thalpha_rec),
    `beta t1/2 (min)` = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", thbeta, thbeta_rec),
    `Input amount (% x L)` = sprintf("%.3f", dose)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table 3 macro-constants (printed / recovered from the packaged model).")

stopifnot(
  # Closed-form round trip on the same numbers: only floating-point error.
  all(abs(recovered$A_rec / recovered$A - 1) < 1e-5),
  all(abs(recovered$B_rec / recovered$B - 1) < 1e-5),
  all(abs(recovered$thalpha_rec / recovered$thalpha - 1) < 1e-5),
  all(abs(recovered$thbeta_rec / recovered$thbeta - 1) < 1e-5)
)
```

The secondary parameters Table 3 prints act as an external check, because they
were averaged across animals separately from the macro-constants:

```{r secondary}
recovered |>
  transmute(
    Site = site_label[model],
    `CL (L/min) printed / packaged` = sprintf("%.2f / %.3f", CL, cl),
    `Vc (L) printed / packaged` = sprintf("%.2f / %.3f", Vc, vc),
    `Vss (L) printed / packaged` = sprintf("%.2f / %.3f", Vss, Vss_rec),
    `MRT (min) printed / packaged` = sprintf("%.2f / %.2f", MRT, MRT_rec)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table 3 secondary parameters against the packaged models.")
```

For the two blood sites the packaged parameters regenerate the printed steady-state
volumes and mean residence times to within 4%, and the pulmonary-artery central
volume to rounding. The **arterial central volume** is printed as 1.09 L, but
with the arterial macro-constants the central volume is fixed at
`Vss * AUC / ((A + B) * MRT)` = `r sprintf("%.3f", recovered$Vc_check[2])` L
from the printed Vss and MRT, whatever the input amount, and 1.09 L is instead the derived *peripheral* volume
(`r sprintf("%.3f", recovered$vp[2])` L = Vss - Vc). The packaged arterial model
therefore uses the central volume implied by the macro-constants; the printed
1.09 L is treated as a transcription slip.

The **end-tidal** means do not hang together as one curve: the beta half-life
is 61.90 +/- 105.93 min, so the mean is pulled by one or more animals with a
long terminal phase, and the reconstructed Vss and MRT exceed the printed means
by 40-65%. The model reproduces the printed end-tidal macro-constants exactly,
but, as the comparisons below show, a curve built from those mean
macro-constants over-predicts the observed end-tidal plateau.

The product `CL x AUC` is close to 48 % x L for all three sites (0.07 x 695.88,
0.08 x 603.03, 0.09 x 533.10), which suggests the fits used one nominal input
amount. The packaged models instead take the amount implied by each site's
printed clearance (the "Input amount" column above). Because the amount and the
volumes scale together, this choice changes the clearance and volumes but not
the predicted concentrations.

# Simulation

The 6% inspiratory exposure is a zero-order infusion of each model's nominal
input amount into `central` over 120 min, followed by 120 min of washout. The
models have no between-subject variability, so a single typical-value profile
per site is the model prediction.

```{r simulate}
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 240, by = 0.5), 121, 123, 125, 130, 140, 180)))

sim <- bind_rows(lapply(des_models, function(m) {
  d <- recovered$dose[recovered$model == m]
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = d, dur = 120, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(obs_times)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[m]], ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  out$model <- m
  out
}))
sim$site <- factor(site_label[sim$model], levels = site_label)
```

## Replicate Figure 3

Table 1 reports the observed mean (SD) at 1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 60 and 120 min of
each phase; Figure 3 shows the same means against the fitted curves.

```{r table1}
t1_times <- c(1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 60, 120)
table1 <- data.frame(
  site = rep(site_label, each = 14),
  time = rep(c(t1_times, 120 + t1_times), 3),
  mean = c(
    # End-tidal (ET), %; '--' at 120 min of disposition (below the 0.2% cutoff)
    3.39, 4.75, 4.93, 5.35, 5.45, 5.61, 5.76, 2.18, 1.23, 1.04, 0.64, 0.38, 0.20, NA,
    # Arterial blood (A), %
    2.75, 3.65, 4.00, 4.17, 4.44, 4.58, 4.65, 2.23, 1.39, 1.24, 0.84, 0.54, 0.32, 0.23,
    # Pulmonary artery blood (PA), %
    1.15, 2.24, 2.61, 3.02, 3.27, 3.62, 4.10, 2.96, 2.08, 1.69, 1.22, 0.85, 0.49, 0.34
  ),
  sd = c(
    0.79, 0.62, 0.23, 0.28, 0.09, 0.09, 0.05, 0.88, 0.47, 0.55, 0.17, 0.10, 0.04, NA,
    0.67, 0.39, 0.53, 0.54, 0.39, 0.40, 0.26, 0.87, 0.43, 0.47, 0.17, 0.07, 0.05, 0.06,
    0.65, 0.45, 0.39, 0.26, 0.34, 0.47, 0.41, 0.54, 0.39, 0.33, 0.23, 0.13, 0.06, 0.05
  )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean))
table1$site <- factor(table1$site, levels = site_label)
```

```{r figure3, fig.height = 8, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Lu 2024: typical-value prediction from the mean Table 3 parameters (line) against the observed means +/- SD from Table 1 (points)."}
ggplot(sim, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_pointrange(
    data = table1,
    aes(time, mean, ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd),
    shape = 1, size = 0.3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~site, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 240, by = 60)) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Desflurane concentration (%)")
```

```{r table1-compare}
cmp <- table1 |>
  left_join(sim |> select(site, time, Cc), by = c("site", "time")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc - mean) / mean)

cmp |>
  mutate(
    Phase = if_else(time <= 120, "uptake", "disposition"),
    `Phase time (min)` = if_else(time <= 120, time, time - 120)
  ) |>
  select(site, Phase, `Phase time (min)`, mean, Cc, pct_diff) |>
  mutate(Cc = signif(Cc, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    "Site" = site,
    "Observed mean (%)" = mean,
    "Model (%)" = Cc,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model prediction against the Table 1 means.")
```

The pulmonary-artery curve tracks the observed means through both phases to
within about 15%. The arterial curve runs 5-15% high on the uptake plateau and
is up to about 30% off the observed means during washout, where the fast
alpha phase (half-life 0.71 min) makes the early disposition points sensitive
to averaging across animals. The end-tidal curve
reaches a plateau far above the 6% inspired concentration, which is physically
impossible for an end-tidal value. This is the averaging artefact described
above, not a property of the measured data.

```{r table1-check}
blood <- cmp |> filter(site != "End-tidal")
stopifnot(
  # Uptake plateau (20-120 min): the blood models sit within ~15% of the
  # observed means. The prediction is deterministic (no random effects).
  all(abs(blood$pct_diff[blood$time %in% c(20, 60, 120)]) < 20),
  # Across all tabulated blood timepoints the centre of the error is modest.
  abs(median(blood$pct_diff)) < 15
)
```

## Validation against the published NCA (PKNCA)

Table 3 reports Cmax and AUC for each site. In a WinNonlin infusion fit the AUC is
the area under the fitted curve to infinity, so it is compared with PKNCA's
`aucinf.obs` on the simulated profile.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(id = 1L, treatment = as.character(site)) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)

dose_df <- recovered |>
  transmute(id = 1L, treatment = site_label[model], time = 0, amt = dose, duration = 120)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
  duration = "duration", route = "intravascular"
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

reference <- tab3 |>
  transmute(treatment = site_label[model], cmax, aucinf.obs)

nca_tbl <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_res, reference,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "aucinf.obs"),
  units = c(cmax = "%", aucinf.obs = "% x min")
)
nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename("Site" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated NCA against Lu 2024 Table 3.")
```

`r attr(nca_tbl, "footnote")`

The two blood models reproduce the printed Cmax and AUC within about 11%; the
residual is the expected gap between a curve built from mean parameters and the
mean of the individual Cmax and AUC values. The end-tidal row is starred for the
reason given above.

```{r nca-check}
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(reference, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_sim", "_ref")) |>
  filter(treatment != "End-tidal")
stopifnot(
  all(abs(nca_wide$cmax_sim / nca_wide$cmax_ref - 1) < 0.15),
  all(abs(nca_wide$aucinf.obs_sim / nca_wide$aucinf.obs_ref - 1) < 0.15)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Typical values only.** Lu 2024 fitted each piglet separately and reported
  the mean and SD of the individual estimates; there is no population model,
  so the packaged models carry no between-subject variability and the
  residual SD is fixed at zero.
* **Parameterisation.** The volumes and intercompartmental clearance are
  derived from the Table 3 macro-constants, with the clearance anchored to the
  printed Table 3 mean. Any other anchor would rescale the volumes and the input
  amount together without changing the predicted concentrations.
* **Input amount.** The paper does not state the dose amount used in the
  WinNonlin fits. Each model's description gives the amount, in % x L, that
  the packaged clearance implies for the 6%, 120-min exposure. Simulating
  other inspired concentrations by scaling the infusion rate in proportion
  assumes the linear zero-order input the authors fitted; the paper studied
  6% only.
* **Arterial central volume.** The printed 1.09 L is inconsistent with the
  arterial macro-constants and equals the derived peripheral volume; the model
  uses the 0.103 L the macro-constants imply.
* **End-tidal model.** Shipped for completeness. Its mean macro-constants
  over-predict the observed end-tidal plateau by about 50% and should not be
  used for quantitative end-tidal simulation. The `compartmentData` specimen
  for its states is "not applicable", because they are curve-fit spaces
  observed through exhaled gas, for which the specimen vocabulary has no member.
* **Concentration units.** All concentrations are percent vapour (the partial
  pressure as a volume percent), as reported. Converting blood values to an
  amount requires the blood-gas partition coefficient (0.38 +/- 0.01 in these
  piglets).
